chunks: From him, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from Uthman al-Asbahani, who said:

Ismail ibn Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) gifted me a bird from the birds of Iraq, so I gifted him a Warshaan (wood-pigeon). So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) entered, saw it, and said: 'The Warshaan is saying,
Blessing be upon you, Blessing be upon you!

key_terms.إِسْمَاعِيلُ بْنُ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Ismail ibn Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the Warshaan bird in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Shia tradition of recognizing divine signs (*ayat*) in nature, where the wood-pigeon’s call is interpreted as a blessing (*bukra*). It reflects the scholarly view that the Imams possessed unique insight into the spiritual realities of creation, turning a simple gift exchange into a moment of theological affirmation.

en.hubeali: From him, from Bakr Bin Salih, from Muhammad Bin Abu Hamza, from Usman Al Asbahany who said,

‘Ismail son of Abu Abdullahasws gifted me a bird from the birds of Al-Iraq, so I gifted to him Al-Warshaan. So Abu Abdullahasws came covered and heasws saw it, so heasws said: ‘The Warshaan is saying, ‘
Blessing be upon you, Blessings be upon you!’,
en.sarwar: 2. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from Bakr ibn Salih from Muhammad ibn abu Hamzah ‘Uthman al-Asbahaniy who has said the following:

“’Isma’il, ibn abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, once, asked me to give a bird of Iraq as a gift to him. I gave him a Warshan. Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, came in. He (the Imam) saw it and said, ‘
Al-Warshan says, ‘You are blessed, you are blessed’
